title: How a Freezer Works in 60 Seconds ❄️🥶 #shorts
description:
A freezer doesn't add cold, it pumps heat out. Liquid refrigerant boils inside cold coils and soaks up heat, a compressor squeezes the hot vapor, and coils outside dump that heat into your kitchen. A fan and thermostat keep the box near minus 18 degrees Celsius. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#freezer #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A freezer doesn't actually make cold. It *pumps heat out* of the box, all day long.

steps.label: Evaporator
steps.text: Inside, liquid *refrigerant* boils in cold coils and soaks up the heat from your food.

steps.label: Compressor
steps.text: A *compressor* then squeezes that vapor, making it hot and high pressure.

steps.label: Condenser
steps.text: Coils on the outside *release the heat* into your kitchen, and the vapor turns back into liquid.

steps.label: Valve
steps.text: A tiny *expansion valve* drops the pressure, so the liquid gets icy cold again.

steps.label: Thermostat
steps.text: A *fan* spreads the cold air, and a thermostat switches the compressor on and off.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Absorb, squeeze, *release*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
